label: Movement invitation line
summary: A line of speech in which a character invites someone to join one of the dynastic cycle's movements.
details: There is one entry per movement (pro-hegemon, expansion, advancement, conservative, undecided) plus a fallback. The four texts shown name the movement through the dynastic cycle situation; two also name the dynasty of whoever holds the empire of China (h_china). The input does not show the condition that picks the entry, nor the texts of the undecided and fallback entries.

label: Isolation reason
summary: The name of a catastrophe: Earthquake, Flood, Plague or Disaster.
details: The four entries show as the words Earthquake, Flood, Plague (for epidemic) and Disaster. Going by its name it gives the reason for an isolation, but the input does not say where it is used or which condition picks which entry.

label: Knight errant animal
summary: The name of an animal: swan, tiger, lion or hart.
details: The input does not show what decides which animal is used, only that the four entries exist.

label: Camp purpose insult
summary: A mocking word for a character's camp purpose, such as hireling for a mercenary or vagabond for a wanderer.
details: Six entries exist (mercenary, wanderer, scholar, explorer, freebooter, legitimist). The input shows the texts of the first four: hireling, vagabond, layabout, rambler. The game may pick randomly among entries whose conditions hold.

label: Camp purpose name
summary: The plain word for a character's camp purpose, such as mercenary, wanderer, scholar or explorer.
details: Six entries exist (the last two are freebooter and legitimist, whose texts the input does not show). It is the neutral counterpart of the insult, plural and article versions, which list the same six purposes.

label: Camp purpose article
summary: The word "a" or "an" that goes in front of the camp purpose name.
details: Five of the six entries give "a" and the fourth gives "an". If the entries run in the same order as GetLaampDescribeTypeSelf, the "an" is for explorer; the input does not state this.

label: Camp purpose plural
summary: The plural of the camp purpose name: mercenaries, wanderers, scholars, explorers and so on.
details: Six entries exist, matching the singular names. The input shows the texts of the first four.

label: Lass or lad
summary: The word "lass" or "lad".
details: The input does not show the condition that picks one. Lass is the word for a girl and lad the word for a boy.

label: Latest topic
summary: A short phrase naming the subject of a task contract, such as the courteous arts or military matters.
details: The game's documentation lists 18 entries, two phrases per topic (diplomacy, martial, stewardship, intrigue, learning, travel, pilgrimage, point of interest, generic). It is marked random valid, so one of the valid phrases can be picked at random. The input gives texts only for the diplomacy and martial entries.

label: Laugh
summary: A written laugh such as "He-he-he!", "Heh!" or "Ho-ho-ho!".
details: There are 11 laughs (the keys include baha, haha, cackle, wheeze and snort). It is marked random valid, so the game can pick any valid one at random. The input shows the texts of the first four only.

label: Learning building
summary: The name of a learning-themed building, such as the Temple, University or Monasteries.
details: Ten entries, from ordinary buildings to special ones (Buddhas of Bamian, Petra, Notre Dame, Hagia Sophia and some holy site buildings, going by the keys). It is marked random valid, so one valid entry can be chosen at random. One text refers to c_bamian through a $c_bamian$ placeholder.

label: Legendary building name
summary: A name for a building in a province, such as a shrine, palace, hall, statue, tower or lodge.
details: This works on a province and has 37 entries (the game's documentation lists them; one key appears twice). The four texts shown are built from the province or its county's faith (for example its high god), as in a great shrine named after the province. The first entry takes its text from a stored localized text named leg_b_name. Going by the name and the keys (leg, figures, dynasty), it is for legendary buildings, but the input does not say so.

label: Fur color
summary: A color word for fur: black, blue or white.
details: The game's documentation lists the scope as all, so it can be used from any scope. The input does not show what picks the color. The name suggests it is meant for a legendary creature, but that is not stated.

label: Liege parade type
summary: The name of a parade type: Military Parade, Cultural Parade or Religious Parade.
details: It has the same three entries as GetParadeType. The name suggests it is meant for the character's liege, but the input does not show how it differs.

label: Liege or "you"
summary: Either the word "you" in a highlight style, or the game's liege concept link.
details: The two entries are CHARACTER_NAME_ME, which shows "you" with a text style tag, and LIEGE, which shows the liege concept. The input does not show the condition that chooses.

label: Liege or "your"
summary: Either "your" or the game's possessive liege concept link (the liege's).
details: The possessive companion of GetLiegeYou: CHARACTER_NAME_MY shows "your" and LIEGE_POSSESSIVE shows the liege possessive concept.

label: Wanderer boost percentage
summary: A percentage that rises with an education rank from 1 to 5: 10%, 20%, 30%, 40% for ranks 1 to 4.
details: The input shows the texts for ranks 1 to 4 only; the rank 5 text is not shown. What the percentage boosts is not stated.

label: A fowl
summary: "a duck", "a chicken", "a rooster" or "a goose", with the article included.
details: Marked random valid, so one of the valid birds can be picked at random.

label: Local commoner
summary: A word for an ordinary person: tribesman, tribeswoman, villagers, townsman, townswoman, peasant or commoner.
details: Seven entries; the input shows the first four texts. The input does not show the conditions that pick one.

label: Local commoners
summary: A plural word for ordinary people: tribespeople, villagers, cityfolk, townsfolk, peasants or commoners.
details: The plural companion of GetLocalCommonerTerm, with six entries.

label: Local role
summary: A word for the character's role: monk or nun, title, culture name or faith adjective.
details: The seven entries are monk, landed, culture, faith, judge, captain and merchant. The texts shown are built from the character: the first uses the NunMonk custom text, the second the title as a name, the third the culture's name and the fourth the faith's adjective.

label: Local street food
summary: The name of a street food from a region, such as sambusa, milkfish skewer, honey fritter or pizza.
details: There are 19 entries (the game's documentation lists all keys; the input shows four texts), covering foods from many regions. Some names go through a Glossary call with its own gloss text.

label: Local street foods
summary: The plural of a regional street food, such as sambusas, milkfish skewers or honey fritters.
details: The plural partner of GetLocalStreetFood, with 19 entries. Note that the tarichos entry has no _plural suffix in its key.

label: Temple word
summary: The word for a faith's house of worship in a province: church, mosque or temple.
details: This works on a province. The three entries are building_temple_church, building_temple_mosque and building_temple_temple.

label: Low official
summary: A title word for a low-ranking noble or local official, such as Archon, tribal elder, seigneur, signore, hidalgo or junker.
details: Nine entries. Some keys name baron, count or nobility titles and culture groups (Byzantine, Arabic); the input does not show the conditions that pick one. The input shows the first four texts.

label: Low officials
summary: The plural of the low-ranking title word, such as tribal elders, archons, seigneurs, signori, walis or magistrates.
details: The plural partner of GetLowOfficial, with nine entries.

label: Lunar New Year animal
summary: The name of one of the twelve Lunar New Year animals, from rat and ox to pig.
details: All twelve animals of the cycle are entries. The input shows the first four texts: monkey, rooster, dog, pig.

label: Men-at-arms type 1
summary: The name of a men-at-arms unit type, such as Bowmen, Light Horsemen, Armored Footmen or Pikemen.
details: Nine entries, including horse archers, light footmen, war elephants and camel riders. GetMAAType2 has the identical entries.

label: Men-at-arms type 2
summary: The name of a men-at-arms unit type, such as Bowmen, Light Horsemen, Armored Footmen or Pikemen.
details: It is identical to GetMAAType1. The input does not say why the game has two; they may let one text name two unit types.

label: Ma or pa
summary: The informal word "ma" for a mother or "pa" for a father.

label: Commons or main square
summary: The word "commons" or "main square", for a public gathering place.
details: The input does not show the condition that picks one.

label: Commons or main square, capitalized
summary: The capitalized form of the gathering place: the commons text again or "Main Square".
details: The first entry reuses the text of is_commons through a $is_commons$ placeholder, so its capitalization is whatever that text has.

label: Mama or papa
summary: The words "mama" for a mother and "papa" for a father.

label: Maneuver
summary: The name of a maneuver, such as Jig, Pivot, Wheelbarrow or Tower.
details: Eleven entries, including plunger, cantilever, animal, plough, hurricane, dangerous animal and knot (from the keys). It is marked random valid, so one valid maneuver can be picked at random.

label: Marginalia drawing
summary: A description of a doodle in a book's margin, such as a tiny knight on a snail.
details: Eight entries (reptile, blob, knight, horse creature, cat, horned man, hounds, sad humans, from the keys). Marked random valid, so one is picked at random.

label: Martial building
summary: The name of a martial-themed building, such as War Camps, Walls & Towers, Hill Forts or Watchtowers.
details: Seven entries, including the Colosseum, the Tower of London and the Citadel of Aleppo (from the keys). Marked random valid.

label: His, her or their
summary: The possessive pronoun his, her or their.
details: The entry keys are CHARACTER_HERHIS_HIS, _HER and _THEIR. The input does not show the condition that picks one.

label: Men, women or warriors
summary: The word men, women or warriors.
details: Warriors is a word that names neither sex, next to the male and female words. The input does not show the condition that picks one.

label: Maternal or paternal
summary: The word "maternal" or "paternal".

label: Medieval dance
summary: The name of a medieval dance such as carole, ring dance, couple dance or estampie.
details: Seven entries; the keys also name syrtos, kerchief and round dances, whose texts the input does not show. Marked random valid.

label: Melee name
summary: The name of the tournament melee: Buhurt or Melee.
details: The entries are tournament_melee_german (Buhurt) and tournament_melee_fallback (Melee). The input does not show the condition for the German one.

label: Merit rank
summary: A glossary link naming a merit rank, such as upper-upper, upper-middle or upper-lower.
details: Ten entries: nine ranks plus a none entry. The four texts shown each give the rank name as a glossary term with its own explanation text.

label: Military appointment law
summary: The name of a succession law: the meritocratic or the celestial appointment law.
details: Each entry returns the name of the matching law (meritocratic_appointment_succession_law or celestial_appointment_succession_law). Going by the key, it is used for military appointments.

label: Drill order
summary: A shouted order for a military drill, such as "Form ranks, stand shoulder to shoulder".
details: Eleven drill orders. Marked random valid, so the game can choose one at random.

label: Colored military strength
summary: A military strength text with a soldier icon, in a green, red or gray style.
details: The text comes from the military strength of the scope saved as second. The green entry uses the #P style, the red one #color_light_red and the gray one #low. The input does not show which condition picks which color.

label: Miracle, first set
summary: A phrase telling a miracle or deed told of a character, such as living all their life atop a pillar.
details: Seven entries whose keys name traits (reclusive, irritable, inappetetic, drunkard, contrite, flagellant, improvident). The texts shown use the character's pronouns. Marked random valid.

label: Miracle, second set
summary: A phrase telling another miracle or deed told of a character, such as prophesying the end of the world.
details: Ten entries whose keys name other traits (lunatic, possessed, disfigured, eunuch, blind, herculean, spindly, chaste, garlic, birds). Some texts use the character's pronouns or their faith's devil name. Marked random valid.

label: Monarch of beauty title
summary: A mock-royal title: King or Queen of Beauty and Noblesse, or King or Queen of Grim and Grievance.
details: Four entries: good and bad, each with a _male key (King) and a key without it (Queen). The input does not show the conditions.

label: Mongol honorific
summary: A fearsome adjective used as an honorific: dreaded, dreadful, mighty, fearsome or frightful.
details: Marked random valid, so one is picked at random.

label: Monograph quality
summary: A sentence judging a monograph (a scholarly book): weak, middling or excellent.
details: The three entries range from a largely derivative book to a great reference for generations. Marked random valid.

label: Monograph theme
summary: A phrase for what a monograph is about: the author's home lands, a point of interest, earlier works or a branch of mathematics.
details: Thirteen entries (the game's documentation lists all keys). The four texts shown name the lands around the author's capital at duchy, kingdom or empire level, or the whole realm of the top liege. The other keys name a point of interest, a commentary on earlier works and mathematical topics such as algebraic geometry. Marked random valid.

label: Monograph topic
summary: The field of a monograph: mathematics or geography.
details: Marked random valid.

label: Parent possessive
summary: The possessive "mother's", "father's" or "parent's".
details: The first two reuse the localization texts $mother$ and $father$ with 's added; the third is the neutral "parent's".

label: Motherly or fatherly
summary: The adjective motherly, fatherly or parental.
details: Parental is the neutral form.

label: Mum or dad
summary: The informal words "mum" for a mother and "dad" for a father.

label: Musical instrument
summary: The name of an instrument such as flute, drum, trumpet or harp.
details: Ten instruments; the keys also name lute, fiddle, lyre, tambourine, bagpipe and hurdy-gurdy, whose texts the input does not show. Marked random valid.

label: Musical instruments
summary: The plural of an instrument name: flutes, drums, trumpets, harps and so on.
details: The plural partner of GetMusicalInstrument with the same ten instruments. Marked random valid.

label: Church power name
summary: The name of a power group in the Christian church situation, such as the clerical or regular rulers of the main power.
details: Seven entries: clerical and regular, each for the main power, the secondary powers and the heretics, plus a fallback. The four texts shown each return the name of the top participant group with the matching key in the_christian_church. The key says "my", so it is probably the group the character belongs to, but the input does not show the conditions.

label: Movement name
summary: The name of a movement in the dynastic cycle situation.
details: Entries for the pro-hegemon, expansion, advancement and conservative movements, undecided, and a fallback. The four texts shown each return the name of the matching top participant group of dynastic_cycle. The key says "my", so it is probably the character's own movement, but the input does not show the conditions or the undecided and fallback texts.

label: Mythical founder
summary: The name of a legendary or historical figure or group, such as Alexander the Great or Charles the Hammer.
details: There are 37 entries (the game's documentation lists all keys), from Arthur, Romulus and Aeneas to Genghis and Odin, plus a fallback. The input does not say where the name is used; going by the key it is a founder figure. Marked random valid.

label: Negative chant
summary: A rude chant shouted at a tournament contestant.
details: Five entries. Two of the four texts shown use the character's titled first name and mock their jousting. Marked random valid, so one is picked at random. The text is crude in places.

label: Insulting chant
summary: A chant that mocks a contestant's weight ("Who ate all the pies?").
details: Only one entry exists.

label: Niece or nephew
summary: The word "niece" or "nephew".

label: No guests message
summary: A court window message saying nobody is there: no courtiers available, or no guests and courtiers.
details: The first says none of the court owner's courtier word (plural) are available at the moment. The second says there are no guests or courtiers, and adds that more may appear over time or can be invited with the decisions above. Both use the court owner's courtier word.

label: Notable characteristic
summary: An adjective for what a person is known for, such as beautiful, handsome, charming or intelligent.
details: Ten entries (the keys also name brave, pious, strong, learned, fierce, wellborn). The two beauty keys, nc_fbeauty and nc_mbeauty, give beautiful and handsome. Marked random valid.

label: Oath
summary: The name of an oath, such as Secure Alliances or Expand the Realm.
details: There are 18 entries (alliance, children, reconquer, conquest, peace, building, university, and more), ending in a no-oath entry. The reconquer text reads the title saved in the player's variable oath_reconquest_title and shows that title's tier name (for example kingdom), as in "Consolidate the" plus the tier.

label: Oath, specific
summary: The name of an oath, as in GetOath but without a no-oath entry.
details: It has 17 entries, the same as GetOath minus GetNoOathText.

label: Object on the nose
summary: The name of an object balanced on a nose: dagger, sword sheath, shoe, chicken, and so on.
details: The keys also name other birds, a candle, a roast swan and signature weapons. Marked random valid.

label: Old book
summary: The name of an old book: Slavic Bible, Greek Bible, Latin poetry book or Greek historiography.
details: Five entries (greek, abrahamic, pagan, eastern, general). The key names and the texts do not seem to match: old_book_greek shows Slavic Bible and old_book_abrahamic shows Greek Bible.

label: Dangerous animals
summary: The plural of an animal type: lions, tigers, leopards, boars and so on.
details: Nine entries; the keys also name hyenas, lynxes, wolves, bears and dogs. The name suggests animals that have got out of control, but the input does not say where it is used.

label: Celestial omen
summary: A description of a sign in the sky, such as a reddened moon or a comet with twin tails.
details: Seven entries (blood moon, star host, comet, falling stars, moon halo, eclipse, wandering star, from the keys). Marked random valid.

label: Own papal score, pious
summary: A line telling the player's own pious papal score, or why they cannot be put forward.
details: The first two entries explain that the college of cardinals cannot name them (rite doctrine bars lay clergy, or clerical gender doctrine excludes their gender). The third shows the score from the script value pam_papal_pious_priority_value. The last has an empty text.

label: Own papal score, populist
summary: A line telling the player's own populist papal score, or why they cannot be put forward.
details: The same as the pious version, but the score line uses pam_papal_populist_priority_value.

label: Own papal score, powerful
summary: A line telling the player's own powerful papal score, or why they cannot be put forward.
details: The same as the pious version, but the score line uses pam_papal_powerful_priority_value.

label: Parade type
summary: The name of a parade type: Military Parade, Cultural Parade or Religious Parade.
details: The civil entry shows the word Cultural.

label: Period of time
summary: A loose phrase for how long something took, from a few days to over a year.
details: Eleven entries; the texts shown are a few days, a week, a fortnight and nearly three weeks, and the keys go on to month, two months, a few months, half a year, year, over a year and a fallback.

label: Petitioner title
summary: How a petitioner is described to their liege: council title, held positions, landed title or courtier.
details: The first three build the text from the character (council title, held court and council positions, title as a name). The last is the plain word courtier.

label: Petition type
summary: The request text of a petition to the liege, such as asking for a council seat or a court position.
details: There are 25 entries (the game's documentation lists all keys) covering council seats, court positions, governorships, debt, war aid, county matters, titles, construction, development, house fiefs, regent, appointment, privilege and gold. The regent key appears twice. Marked random valid.

label: Pilgrim or hajji trait
summary: A bullet list line naming a pilgrimage trait: hajjaj for a hajj, pilgrim for a pilgrimage.
details: Each text also says that the gallowsbait trait is lost during a pious hajj or pilgrimage. The pilgrim one also mentions the trait's experience track.

label: Pilgrim or pilgrims
summary: The word "pilgrim" or "pilgrims".

label: Pilgrim XP, tier 0
summary: The pilgrim trait experience reward for the lowest tier, shown as a number.
details: It shows the script value pilgrimage_low_pious_trait_xp_value.

label: Pilgrim XP, tier 1
summary: The pilgrim trait experience reward for the middle tier, shown as a number.
details: It shows the script value pilgrimage_mid_pious_trait_xp_value.

label: Pilgrim XP, tier 2
summary: The pilgrim trait experience reward for the high tier, shown as a number.
details: It shows the script value pilgrimage_high_pious_trait_xp_value.

label: Pilgrim XP, tier 3
summary: The pilgrim trait experience reward for the perfect tier, shown as a number.
details: It shows the script value pilgrimage_perfect_pious_trait_xp_value.

label: Pious adjective
summary: A word for religious devotion: pious, sacred, holy, devout, religious or saintly.
details: Marked random valid.

label: Pious or believers
summary: The word "pious" or the words "strong believers".

label: Pilgrim flavor, tier 0
summary: A short first-person quote at the lowest pilgrimage tier: a pious one or a worldly one.
details: The pious line mentions appeasing the faith's pantheon term; the worldly line is about seeing other cultures.

label: Pilgrim flavor, tier 1
summary: A short first-person quote at the middle pilgrimage tier: a pious one or a worldly one.
details: The pious line says the divine smiles; the worldly line speaks of sights still to see.

label: Pilgrim flavor, tier 2
summary: A short first-person quote at the high pilgrimage tier: a pious one or a worldly one.
details: The pious line is about almost transcending; the worldly line about the many things experienced.

label: Pilgrim flavor, tier 3
summary: A short first-person quote at the perfect pilgrimage tier: a pious one or a worldly one.
details: The pious line says spirit and the divine are one; the worldly line says the world has been tasted.

label: Pilgrim rewards, tier 0
summary: A bullet list of the rewards of the lowest pilgrimage tier, pious or worldly.
details: The pious text gives a piety activity reward percentage and pilgrim trait experience. The worldly text gives a cultural acceptance reward percentage; a third entry lists the low worldly reward modifier.

label: Pilgrim rewards, tier 1
summary: A bullet list of the rewards of the middle pilgrimage tier, pious or worldly.
details: Same structure as tier 0 with the mid values: piety and trait experience, cultural acceptance, and the mid worldly reward modifier.

label: Pilgrim rewards, tier 2
summary: A bullet list of the rewards of the high pilgrimage tier, pious or worldly.
details: Same structure as tier 0 with the high values: piety and trait experience, cultural acceptance, and the high worldly reward modifier.

label: Pilgrim rewards, tier 3
summary: A bullet list of the rewards of the perfect pilgrimage tier, pious or worldly.
details: Same structure as tier 0 with the perfect values: piety and trait experience, cultural acceptance, and the perfect worldly reward modifier.

label: Plague effect
summary: A fanciful symptom, such as to spit fire, sprout another limb or grow a third eye.
details: Eight entries; the keys also name a third nipple, blue, hairy, fingernails and eyes. Marked random valid. The texts are verb phrases. The name suggests the symptoms of a plague.

label: Positive chant
summary: A cheering chant shouted at a tournament contestant.
details: Four entries. Some use the character's full name or short possessive name. Marked random valid.

label: Dangerous terrain feature
summary: A description of how the ground becomes dangerous in a province, depending on its terrain.
details: This works on a province. There are 15 terrain entries (desert, mountains, forest, wetlands and so on); the input shows four texts, such as "sands shift unpredictably". Marked random valid.

label: Preferred topic
summary: A short phrase naming a subject, such as the courteous arts or the art of warfare.
details: Sixteen entries, two per topic, as in GetLatestTopic but without the generic topic. Going by the name, it is a subject a character prefers. Marked random valid.

label: Preferred topic concept
summary: The game concept link for a topic, such as diplomacy, martial, stewardship or intrigue.
details: Eight entries, one per topic (also learning, travel, pilgrimage, point of interest).

label: Pretty adjective
summary: A word for good looks: pretty, comely, radiant, handsome, striking, fetching, winsome or fair.
details: Marked random valid.
